predecessors.name: Russian Empire
predecessors.text: Syr-Darya and Semirechye oblasts, the first two oblasts of the governor-generalship, carved out of the Russian conquests of 1865-66 and the Steppe governor-generalship

predecessors.name: Khanate of Kokand
predecessors.text: Tashkent, Chimkent and the Syr Darya oblast taken 1865-66; the Fergana rump in 1876

predecessors.name: Emirate of Bukhara
predecessors.text: Samarkand and the Zeravshan valley, Jizzakh and Ura-Tepe

predecessors.name: Khanate of Khiva
predecessors.text: the Amu Darya Division on the right bank

successors.name: Turkestan ASSR
successors.text: the whole governor-generalship: the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic proclaimed 30 April 1918 at Tashkent

ledger.x: 1867: Khujand, Jizzakh and Ura-Tepe are in Russian hands since 1866 ('Romanovsky turned east and took Khujand'; 'took Jizzakh from Bukhara'; 'took Ura-Tepe').
1867: Russia forms the Turkestan Governor-Generalship at Tashkent.
1868: Samarkand and the Zeravshan valley pass to Russia.
1873: the Amu Darya Division is annexed from Khiva.
1876: Kokand is abolished and the Fergana Oblast formed.
1882: Semirechye passes to the Steppe governor-generalship.
1886: the governor-generalship is also called the Turkestan Krai.
1897: the Transcaspian Oblast joins the governor-generalship.
1918: the Turkestan republic replaces the governor-generalship; whether Bukhara's protectorate (and Khiva's, below) passed to it is on no page (the TASSR page 'does not describe their relationship').
1918: as for Bukhara; the khanate falls in February 1920 (khanate-of-khiva dossier).
1918: the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic is proclaimed at Tashkent.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Central Asia
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Kokand abolished (1876), Bukhara and Khiva made protectorates (1868, 1873), Transcaspia annexed (1881-84); the Afghan frontier delimited after Panjdeh (1885).

wars.name: Central Asian revolt of 1916
wars.outcome: Suppressed; 'Order had not fully been restored by the time the February Revolution took place in 1917.'

certainty.note: Steppe and desert frontiers; the Chinese frontier follows the 1864 Treaty of Tarbagatai ('roughly set the current Chinese-Kazakh border', RC) and the Bukhara and Khiva lines are approximate.
The Afghan frontier was delineated 1885-86 after Panjdeh (RC) and the Pamirs border was settled in the 1890s; the Bukhara and Khiva protectorate lines stay approximate.
